counterfactual_missing_items: R3 has no raw span linking the healthy forearm patch to 35.0% wild-type transcripts in the potentially revertant epidermis
R3 does not address the restricted epidermal reversion pattern that distinguishes revertant mosaicism from general dystrophic EB
No raw contradiction or alternative diagnostic pattern was present to displace the revertant-mosaicism diagnosis
decisive_items: Potentially revertant area epidermis: High rates of wild-type transcripts (35.0%)
compound heterozygous alterations (c.2992 + 2T>G and c.8621-30A>G) at splice sites in COL7A1
A patch of healthy skin (7.5 × 4 cm²) on the left forearm, lacking blistering
response.rationale: R1 and R3 share the same COL7A1 splice-site evidence, so that finding is not discriminative. R1 adds the decisive raw observation of high wild-type transcripts in the potentially revertant epidermis and connects it to the cutaneous healthy patch, yielding the specific diagnosis of revertant mosaicism in dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa. R3 remains the broader umbrella diagnosis and does not explain the revertant wild-type transcript data, so R3 is a genuine but less complete candidate.

rejected.why: R3 captures the causative COL7A1 defect and ulcer pattern but misses the revertant mosaicism evidenced by the high wild-type transcript rate in the healthy forearm epidermis.
